newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Proton, shareholder buy 80 pct of Lotus.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Proton, shareholder buy 80 pct of Lotus.

text.p: Malaysian national carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) and its chairman, Yahaya Ahmad, have bought an 80 percent stake in British sports car maker Group Lotus Ltd, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.
The news agency quoted a Proton statement as saying the deal was valued at 51 million pounds ($82.88 million).
Proton bought a 63.75 percent stake or 6.375 million Lotus shares for 38 million pounds, and Yahaya acquired 16.25 percent or 1.625 million shares for 13 million pounds.
Yahaya is the controlling shareholder and chairman of Proton.
Bernama said that under the agreement, Proton would lend Lotus 13 million pounds at a rate of 1.5 percent per annum over the Midland Bank Base Rate ruling, from day-to-day for a one-year period.
The Proton statement said the acquisition would be funded from internally generated funds.
The acquisition was subject to approval from the Malaysian central bank, Bank Negara, but did not need shareholders' approval, it said.
"The acquisition would...avail Proton ready access to research and development capability, thus saving on financial resources, time and manpower," Proton said.
The statement confirmed market speculation that Proton was seeking to take a majority stake in the British car maker.
Lotus was taken over by General Motors Corp in 1986, and then piled up losses of 50 million pounds in the five years before its sale in 1993 to Bugatti International.
On Wednesday, South Korea's Daewoo Motor Co Ltd, a unit of Daewoo Group, said it has shelved plans to buy a stake in Lotus after an earlier bid.
